title: UK labour market overview — earnings, unemployment and vacancies (ONS, 07:00 London / 02:00 ET), the release the chain spent four documents locating: the first wholly post-Budget AWE window, measured here and found to carry no signal
source: EST: two UK-government primaries RE-FETCHED direct 2026-09-10 by this event's own lane, both HTTP 200, rather than inherited from the proposal. (1) gov.uk/government/statistics/announcements/uk-labour-market-march-2027 — the statutory pre-announcement register reads 'UK Labour Market: March 2027', '16 March 2027 7:00am (confirmed)', producer Office for National Statistics, designation 'Accredited official statistics', announcement page published 30 June 2026, contents 'employment, unemployment, inactivity, average weekly earnings, vacancies and other labour market related statistics for the UK'. (2) ons.gov.uk/releases/uklabourmarketmarch2027 — the ONS release calendar reads 'UK Labour Market: March 2027', '16 March 2027 at 7:00am', 'Not yet published'. Filed estimate per this lane's no-self-confirm limit and because the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts carries BLS:/BEA:/CENSUS:/FED: and has no slot for the UK Office for National Statistics — the same gap all six 2026-27 siblings were filed under. The DATE is not in doubt; the estimate label is about the taxonomy, not the evidence
notes: RESEARCHED 2026-09-10 by its own lane (docs/research/events/uk-labour-market-2027-03-16.md), which read the single proposal in full — proposals/uk-labour-market-2027-03-16.from-uk-labour-market-2027-01-19.json, now inert and left in place — and re-fetched every primary rather than inheriting it. THE TITLE IS CHANGED, AND THE CHANGE IS THE HEADLINE FINDING. THE DESTINATION IS CONFIRMED; THE MILESTONE IS EMPTY. (1) The chain's arithmetic is RIGHT, and this lane raised its grade rather than repeating its method. Four sibling ledgers argued about which ONS release first carries an average-weekly-earnings window wholly after the 2026-10-28 Budget; 11-17 and 12-15 refuted the claim for their own prints, and both the 12-15 ledger's leg 8 and the proposal that created uk-labour-market-2027-01-19 named 'the FEBRUARY 2027 release'; the 01-19 lane corrected that to THIS release by rolling the window rule forward from the August 2026 bulletin. This lane settled it from the SAME-MONTH ANCHOR read firsthand instead of from a rolled habit: the 19 March 2026 bulletin (ons.gov.uk, fetched 2026-09-10) carries 'November 2025 to January 2026' AWE and LFS, 'December 2025 to February 2026' vacancies and a February 2026 payroll flash. A March release is exactly where a Nov-Jan window lands. So THIS release carries NOV 2026-JAN 2027 AWE/LFS, DEC 2026-FEB 2027 vacancies and a FEBRUARY 2027 payroll flash, and it is the first AWE window with no pre-Budget day in it. (2) AND THE MILESTONE CARRIES NO MEASURED INFORMATION, WHICH IS THIS LANE'S CONTRIBUTION AND ITS CALL. Measured firsthand on the ONS's own private-sector regular-pay series (KAJ4, three-month-average year-on-year, seasonally adjusted, excluding arrears; ons.gov.uk timeseries /data endpoint, HTTP 200, 304 monthly observations from 2001; the current vintage reproduces the published Apr-Jun 2026 bulletin figures exactly — private 2.8, whole economy 3.5 via KAI9, public 6.1 via KAJ7), across the FOUR Autumn Budgets with data the change at the first-wholly-post-Budget boundary was +0.2pp (2017-11-22), +0.4pp (2021-10-27), -0.3pp (2024-10-30) and -0.1pp (2025-11-26). Signed mean +0.05pp, t(3) = 0.32. Mean absolute 0.25pp against an ordinary-month mean of 0.183pp and a standard deviation of 0.245pp over 287 non-COVID months. THE SIGN IS 2-2 — A COIN FLIP. At n=4 the test can only detect an effect of about 0.49pp, and it is stated that way rather than dressed as a null. (3) THE VENUE THAT IS NOT EMPTY IS APRIL, AND IT IS PROPOSED IN THIS PR. UK employer-cost measures conventionally take effect the following April (the 11-17 lane's precedent: Autumn Budget 2024-10-30 raised secondary Class 1 NICs 13.8% to 15% effective April 2025), so a 2026-10-28 Budget bites in APRIL 2027, which is outside this release's Nov-Jan window entirely. The first window CONTAINING that April is Feb-Apr 2027, published 2027-06-15 ('15 June 2027 7:00am (confirmed)', gov.uk register fetched today) — proposed here as uk-labour-market-2027-06-15.from-uk-labour-market-2027-03-16.json because it is where a Budget effect would appear if anywhere. At that boundary the same four Budgets gave 0.0, -0.1, -0.4 and -0.1pp: no positive in four, which is directionally consistent where the announcement boundary is a coin flip, but every one of them is inside ordinary noise and a 3-of-3 sign test is p = 0.125. (4) THE CORRIDOR INVERTS THE JANUARY SIBLING'S. Seven tracked events sit within five days and TWO ARE HIGH-IMPACT: fomc-2027-03-17 at D+1 and opex-2027-03-19 at D+3, with boj-decision-2027-03-18 (medium) at D+2, plus vix-expiration-2027-03-17, tic-monthly-2027-03-18, japan-cpi-2027-03-19 and sp-rebalance-reference-close-2027-03-12. fomc-blackout-start-2027-03-06 sits at D-10, so the print lands INSIDE a Fed blackout on the eve of an FOMC decision. The 01-19 sibling had the thinnest corridor of five entries; this one is the loudest, and it makes attribution worse, not better. (5) THE MPC ROUND IS D+2 AND IT IS A NON-REPORT ROUND, read firsthand: bankofengland.co.uk/monetary-policy/upcoming-mpc-dates lists 'Thursday 18 March' as 'March MPC Summary and minutes', provisional — the same D-2-into-a-non-Report geometry the 12-15 lane already settled from the March and June 2026 precedents, so it is NOT re-registered here. Note it falls the day AFTER the FOMC. UK CPI is 2027-03-24 (proposal only), EIGHT days later, so unlike January the UK data run is not two consecutive days. IMPACT LOW, argued not inherited: symbols [], this repo tracks no UK-listed symbol, no house playbook is rates- or sterling-keyed, and the measured cable reaction to the 2026-08-18 release was ~0.1% on a two-sided beat. Estimate widens caution only; nothing date-keyed may act on this.
